answer: The hypothesis receives some positive support, but not consistent support across specifications: 42 of 256 universes (16.4%) show a statistically supported positive effect, while 214 (83.6%) are indeterminate and none show a statistically supported negative effect. The conclusion depends materially on how race groups and contraband hits are defined, so the broad hypothesis should be narrowed.
rationale: Positive evidence exists and the overall standardized-effect median is positive (0.0456), but most specifications are non-significant or otherwise indeterminate. Substantive choices about the comparison population and outcome definition produce large effect changes and inference flips, preventing a robust conclusion for the broad claim.
key_evidence: 42 of 256 universes have statistically significant positive effects; 214 are indeterminate and 0 are significantly negative.
The standardized effect has median 0.0456, with the middle 50% ranging from 0.0067 to 0.2585 and a minimum of -0.0010.

Race-sample definitions have substantially different option medians: 0.0069 for Black-versus-White-only, 0.2833 when unknown and other groups are included as non-Black, and 0.2594 using raw race mapping.
Contraband coding produces a 36.4% inference-flip rate; its option medians are 0.0069 for direct-field coding and 0.1321 for the drug-or-weapon union.
refinement_reason: The broad claim combines materially different comparison populations and outcome definitions. These choices change the estimated effect and, for contraband coding, change inference in 36.4% of paired specifications.
suggested_hypotheses: Among searched stops classified strictly as Black or White, Black subjects have a higher rate of direct-field contraband hits than White subjects.
Among searched stops using the drug-or-weapon union as the contraband outcome, Black subjects have a higher hit rate than the specified comparison group.
Using raw race fields to classify Black and White subjects and a prespecified contraband definition, Black subjects have a higher hit rate than White subjects.
caveats: Non-significance does not establish no effect; the 214 indeterminate universes may reflect limited precision.
Inference changes under uncertainty choices, with an 18.3% overall inference-flip rate and a 27.5% flip rate when clustering by department versus officer or treating stops as independent.
The supplied effects are reported on a standardized scale, so they do not by themselves provide the raw Black and White hit rates.

race_analytic_sample.label: Race groups included
race_analytic_sample.rationale: Which recorded driver races should define the Black-versus-White comparison?  [found by: direct]

black_white_only.label: Black and White subjects only
black_white_only.description: Retain rows where `subject_race` is exactly `black` or `white`; exclude `hispanic`, `asian/pacific islander`, `other`, `unknown`, and missing values.

use_raw_race_mapping.label: Use raw race fields to classify Black and White
use_raw_race_mapping.description: Classify subjects using `raw_Race` (and, if needed, `raw_Ethnicity`) according to the source codes; retain only source-coded Black and White subjects, excluding other or ambiguous codes.

include_unknown_as_nonwhite.label: Black versus all non-Black subjects
include_unknown_as_nonwhite.description: Retain Black subjects as the exposed group and combine White, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, Other, Unknown, and missing `subject_race` values into the comparison group.

searched_stop_definition.label: Definition of a searched stop
searched_stop_definition.rationale: Which rows count as searched stops for the denominator?  [found by: direct]

search_conducted.label: Recorded conducted search
search_conducted.description: Retain rows with `search_conducted == 1`; exclude all rows with `search_conducted == 0` or missing.

person_or_vehicle_search.label: Person or vehicle search indicator
person_or_vehicle_search.description: Retain rows with `search_person == 1` or `search_vehicle == 1`; exclude rows where both indicators are 0 or missing.

any_search_related_action.label: Any search-related action
any_search_related_action.description: Retain rows with `search_conducted == 1`, `search_person == 1`, `search_vehicle == 1`, or `frisk_performed == 1`; treat a row as searched if any of these indicators equals 1.

contraband_hit_coding.label: Any-contraband outcome coding
contraband_hit_coding.rationale: How should `contraband_found`, `contraband_drugs`, and `contraband_weapons` define a hit among selected searched stops?  [found by: direct]

direct_contraband_complete_case.label: Direct contraband field, complete cases
direct_contraband_complete_case.description: Define a hit as `contraband_found == TRUE` and a non-hit as `contraband_found == FALSE`; exclude selected searched rows where `contraband_found` is missing.

direct_contraband_missing_nonhit.label: Direct contraband field, missing as no hit
direct_contraband_missing_nonhit.description: Define a hit as `contraband_found == TRUE`; define every other selected searched row, including missing `contraband_found`, as a non-hit.

drug_or_weapon_union.label: Union of drugs and weapons fields
drug_or_weapon_union.description: Define a hit if `contraband_drugs == TRUE` or `contraband_weapons == TRUE`; define a non-hit if both are FALSE; exclude rows where both component fields are missing.

date_scope.label: Calendar scope of recorded stops
date_scope.rationale: Which dates in the supplied rows should enter the analysis?  [found by: direct]

all_supplied_rows.label: All supplied rows
all_supplied_rows.description: Use every row passing the race, searched-stop, and outcome rules, regardless of the value of `date`; do not impose an additional date filter.

stated_2002_2015_window.label: Stops dated 2002 through 2015
stated_2002_2015_window.description: Retain only rows whose parsed `date` is between `2002-01-01` and `2015-12-31`, inclusive; exclude missing, invalid, and out-of-window dates.

complete_date_only.label: All rows with valid dates
complete_date_only.description: Retain all rows with a successfully parsed `date`, including dates outside 2002–2015; exclude only missing or invalid dates.

race_comparison_model.label: Statistical comparison of hit rates
race_comparison_model.rationale: Should the Black-versus-White comparison use raw rates or adjust for observed stop and driver characteristics?  [found by: direct]

unadjusted_rate_comparison.label: Unadjusted two-group rate comparison
unadjusted_rate_comparison.description: For each race, calculate hits divided by selected searched stops and compare the two proportions without adjustment for `subject_age`, `subject_sex`, `reason_for_stop`, `department_name`, officer, date, or time.

race_only_logistic.label: Race-only logistic model
race_only_logistic.description: Fit `hit ~ Black`, where `hit` is the coded any-contraband outcome and Black indicates `subject_race == black` versus `white`; report the race coefficient as the comparison.

adjusted_logistic.label: Observed-characteristics adjusted logistic model
adjusted_logistic.description: Fit `hit ~ Black + subject_age + subject_sex + reason_for_stop + department_name + calendar_year`, using complete cases for these predictors; report the adjusted Black coefficient, with `calendar_year` derived from `date`.

dependence_and_uncertainty.label: Dependence structure for uncertainty
dependence_and_uncertainty.rationale: How should repeated stops associated with the same officer or department affect standard errors and the hypothesis test?  [found by: direct]

independent_stops.label: Treat stops as independent
independent_stops.description: Compute uncertainty as if each searched stop were independent, with no clustering adjustment for `officer_id_hash` or `department_name`.

cluster_officer.label: Cluster by officer
cluster_officer.description: Use cluster-robust uncertainty with `officer_id_hash` as the clustering unit, allowing arbitrary dependence among stops handled by the same officer.

cluster_department.label: Cluster by department
cluster_department.description: Use cluster-robust uncertainty with `department_name` as the clustering unit, allowing arbitrary dependence among stops reported by the same department.
